prompt.context: Our client is a bank in the US. It has a large retail footprint and offers a mix of services to end-customers (checking, debit, credit cards). They also have loan centers to sell mortgages in the same markets. The bank currently serves 15 million customers. Our client has historically been profitable, but increased regulation and the downturn in the economy have caused the bank to see a sharp decline in profitability. The client has engaged us to help determine next steps for its business and has asked us to assess ways they can increase profits within the next 12 months.
prompt.question: What are ways the bank can increase profits within the next 12 months?

clarifying_info.q: How does the bank earn its profits?
clarifying_info.a: The bank earns profits primarily through the spread between what it lends money out at and its borrowing costs, as well as fees on various services such as checking, debit, and credit cards.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any constraints on the solutions we should consider?
clarifying_info.a: No specific constraints have been given beyond the 12-month horizon. Both cost reduction and revenue increase strategies are in scope.

exhibits.title: Our client has 5 distinct groups of customers
exhibits.shows: A waterfall-style chart breaking down annual $ per customer for five customer groups (Group 1 through Group 5), showing revenue potential, margin from banking costs, transaction costs, cost to serve, and resulting profit per group, alongside the percentage of total clients each group represents.

framework: Use a Profitability framework: Profit = Revenue - Costs
Revenue levers: Price (fees, rates) and Quantity (current customers, new customers, product mix)
Cost levers: Fixed costs (branches, headcount) and Variable costs (transaction costs)
Prioritize short-term actions achievable within 12 months
Assess trade-offs and risks for each lever

questions.prompt: 1. What are some of the ways the bank can increase profits in the next 12 months?
questions.guidance: A strong answer is structured and covers both cost reduction and revenue growth with clear examples. Candidate should apply a Profitability framework.

questions.prompt: 2. What are some of the risks with shutting down branch locations?
questions.guidance: Look for structure in the response. Near-term risks: poor PR, legal/contractual complications, extra costs (severance), loss of customers who bank through that branch, asset sales scaring investors. Long-term risks: what happens when the market rebounds and the bank lacks physical presence?

questions.prompt: 3. What segments do you think a retail bank has?
questions.guidance: Look for clear delineation between profitable and unprofitable customers with characteristics of each. Example: Segment 1 is mass-affluent, highly profitable, uses checking + money market + mortgage, low transaction cost (ATM/internet). Segment 2 is lower income, small checking balance, heavy teller and call-center usage.

questions.prompt: 4. Look at Exhibit 1 and walk me through what the bank is experiencing.
questions.guidance: Key insights: only 30% of customers (Groups 4 and 5) are currently profitable; 20% of customers (Group 2) have low revenue potential and high transaction costs making them deeply unprofitable (-$25/customer); Groups 1 and 3 also lose money. The client needs to change the mix of products from Groups 1 and 2 and address high transaction costs.

questions.prompt: 5. What is the average annual profitability per customer?
questions.guidance: Candidate should weight each group's per-customer profit by its percentage of the total customer base and sum the results.

math.setup: Weighted profitability = sum of (Profit per group * % of clients). Total customers = 15,000,000.

questions.prompt: 6. What is the annual bank profitability?
questions.guidance: Multiply average profit per customer by total customers. Push candidate toward a shortcut rather than computing each group individually.

math.setup: Total Profit = Total Customers * Average Profit per Customer

questions.prompt: 7. The bank is considering a $0.85/month ($10/year) checking account fee. Given the expected customer retention rates (Group 1: 60%, Group 2: 40%, Group 3: 20%, Group 4: 60%, Group 5: 50%), what is the new annual profitability per customer and total?
questions.guidance: Compute remaining customers per group, then total profit = profit without fee + fee revenue. Round $0.85/month to $10/year. Candidate may be guided if running short on time.

math.setup: For each group: remaining customers = 15M * % of segment * % that stay. Total profit per group = (remaining customers * profit without fee) + (remaining customers * $10). New average = total profit / new total customers.
steps: Group 1: 15M*30%*60%=2,700K customers; profit without fee=2,700K*(-$5)=-$13,500K; fee revenue=2,700K*$10=$27,000K; total=$13,500K
Group 2: 15M*20%*40%=1,200K customers; profit without fee=1,200K*(-$25)=-$30,000K; fee revenue=1,200K*$10=$12,000K; total=-$18,000K
Group 3: 15M*20%*20%=600K customers; profit without fee=600K*(-$5)=-$3,000K; fee revenue=600K*$10=$6,000K; total=$3,000K
Group 4: 15M*10%*60%=900K customers; profit without fee=900K*$15=$13,500K; fee revenue=900K*$10=$9,000K; total=$22,500K
Group 5: 15M*20%*50%=1,500K customers; profit without fee=1,500K*$45=$67,500K; fee revenue=1,500K*$10=$15,000K; total=$82,500K
math.answer: Total profit = $103,500,000; 6.9 million customers remain; average profit per customer = $15

brainstorming.prompt: What are all the ways the bank can increase profits within 12 months?

categories.name: Reduce Fixed Costs
ideas: Push customers to online channels to reduce headcount needs

categories.name: Reduce Variable Costs
ideas: Move to paperless/digital to reduce transaction costs

categories.name: Increase Revenue - Current Customers
ideas: Cross-sell mortgages, refinancing, credit cards, money market accounts, advisory services
Change product mix toward higher-revenue products

categories.name: Increase Revenue - Price
ideas: Introduce or raise debit card fees
Raise interest rates charged on loans

categories.name: Increase Revenue - New Products
ideas: Launch new financial products targeting profitable segments

recommendation: Institute a $0.85/month ($10/year) checking account fee; this is the quickest way to create new revenue streams while naturally segmenting out deeply unprofitable customers
The fee increases average annual profit per customer from $3 to $15 (5x improvement) and total profit from $45M to $103.5M, even as the customer base drops from 15M to 6.9M
Groups 3 and 2, which were previously loss-making, flip to profitable or near-break-even as high-cost, low-balance customers self-select out
risks: Bad PR from customer backlash (e.g., reputational damage similar to real-world debit fee rollbacks)
High transaction costs in the short term as customers call in or visit branches to understand the fee
Revenue and retention estimates could be off; actual churn may differ from projections
Loss of customers who are currently unprofitable but could become profitable in the future
next_steps: Move forward with instituting the $0.85/month checking fee
Evaluate exempting certain high-value or strategically important groups from the fee
Monitor churn rates against projections and adjust strategy accordingly
Continue exploring branch consolidation and segmentation strategies as complementary initiatives
